identity.headline: Product leader and advisor: co-founder and Chief Product Officer at Native, external advisor to Bain & Company, and advisor to Provenance and Eureka AI. Former Expert Partner at Bain & Company, with earlier analytics leadership at McKinsey & Company and dunnhumby.
identity.selfDescription: Creating intelligent systems: 20+ years building solutions globally to understand behavior and drive action.
identity.biography:
Brock Simon is a product leader and advisor. Since January 2026 he has been co-founder and Chief Product Officer of Native, which describes its work as database reasoning for complex enterprise data. He has also been an external advisor to Bain & Company since January 2026, and an advisor to Provenance and to Eureka AI since December 2025.

Before Native he spent six years at Bain & Company in San Francisco: Expert Associate Partner from June 2019, then Expert Partner from July 2022 to November 2025, where he led AI initiatives, including work with OpenAI, for large enterprise clients. Before Bain he was an Expert Associate Partner at McKinsey & Company, in Chicago from 2015 and in Bangkok from 2017 to 2019. He spent a decade at dunnhumby, from analyst in Cincinnati in 2005 to Head of Solutions for Asia in Shanghai in 2015, by way of Atlanta, Bangkok, Portland and Izmir: he launched the dunnhumby and Tesco international partnership in Thailand, ran the Turkey business as Country Head, and led the establishment of several international markets.

He holds an MBA from Xavier University and a BA and MS in Mathematics and Statistics from Miami University. He lives in the San Francisco Bay Area and has been a seasonal ski coach at Palisades Tahoe since October 2021.
identity.location: San Francisco Bay Area, United States

perspectives.position: The bigger shift in AI shopping is discovery moving upstream, before the shopper reaches a retailer. Systems that ground the difference between a marketing claim and a verified one do not yet exist, and both AI models and shoppers are still in a norming stage.
perspectives.quote: To me, the bigger shift is watching that discovery move upstream

perspectives.position: AI is less experimental than many executives assume. The advance that matters is putting agents on top of existing models, workflows and best practices, with humans in the loop: augmented decision-making is what is winning in the enterprise.
AI has compressed the time from product design to deployment and from insight to execution, which makes data understanding and data engineering the next bottlenecks for enterprises.

faq.question: What connects his retail AI experience to joining Native?
faq.answer: Brock connects his decision to join Native with enterprise-data problems he encountered while working on retail AI.

faq.question: What drew Brock to dunnhumby?
faq.answer: Brock says an interest in understanding real people through transaction and loyalty data drew him to dunnhumby.

faq.question: How did his McKinsey work in Asia differ in emphasis?
faq.answer: Brock describes more of his McKinsey work in Asia as focused on data monetization and coalition loyalty, reflecting the conglomerates he worked with in the region.

faq.question: Is Brock Simon still at Bain & Company?
faq.answer: No. He was Expert Associate Partner at Bain & Company from June 2019 and Expert Partner from July 2022 to November 2025, in San Francisco. Since January 2026 he has been an external advisor to Bain & Company, providing advisory support on select projects, including retail AI work, alongside his role as co-founder and Chief Product Officer of Native.

faq.question: What is Native, and what is his role there?
faq.answer: Native describes its work as database reasoning for complex enterprise data: it helps enterprises understand complex data by reasoning across the data itself, discovering structure, relationships, definitions, exceptions and gaps so teams can build reliable data foundations. Brock Simon is its co-founder and Chief Product Officer since January 2026 and based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Native's company page gives 2025 as its founding year and lists him among its people.

faq.question: What was his title at McKinsey & Company?
faq.answer: Expert Associate Partner, in Chicago from August 2015 to August 2017 and in Bangkok from August 2017 to May 2019, as he records it on LinkedIn. Illinois Tech's Marketing Analytics Advisory Council page recorded the title as Expert associate principal, with a focus on marketing and digital analytics in retail and consumer packaged goods.

faq.question: Where did he study?
faq.answer: Miami University, where he took a BA and an MS in Mathematics and Statistics, and Xavier University, where he took an MBA. Bain's team page and Illinois Tech's council page name the same institutions and word the Miami degrees differently: his own record says a BA and an MS in Mathematics and Statistics, Bain's page an MSc in mathematics and statistics, and Illinois Tech a B.S. in Mathematics and Statistics and an M.S. in Mathematics. His own wording stands until he settles it.

faq.question: Is this the same Brock Simon who worked for dunnhumby in Turkey and Shanghai?
faq.answer: Yes. His decade at dunnhumby, from 2005 to 2015, ran from Cincinnati through Atlanta, Bangkok, Portland and Izmir to Shanghai, ending as Head of Solutions for Asia. Bain's team page and his LinkedIn both record it. This record is not about other people who share the name.

faq.question: What has he written or spoken about?
faq.answer: Three Bain & Company articles in 2025, each co-authored: on data monetisation with AI (first-named of five authors, June 2025), Google Cloud Next (first-named of four, April 2025) and Nvidia GTC (second-named of seven, March 2025); a servicePath Executive Conversations podcast on agentic AI, personalisation, loyalty and data monetisation; a Provenance webinar on AI shopping and verified product data; and the MAUSTRAP Podcast on why he founded Native and how AI changes product decisions. profile.json lists each with its link and its byline.

corrections.statement: Illinois Tech records his McKinsey title as Expert associate principal; his LinkedIn gives Expert Associate Partner. Both are published, LinkedIn's wording leading, as title variants on the McKinsey roles.

Three sources word his degrees differently: his own record says BA and MS in Mathematics and Statistics; Bain's team page says an MSc in mathematics and statistics; Illinois Tech says a B.S. in Mathematics and Statistics and an M.S. in Mathematics. His own wording is published until he settles it.
Native's benchmark results are company results reported by Native, not Brock Simon's personal results. They are recorded as outcomes of the Native programme, never as his achievements.

Trade reports of 22 May 2026 list him on Provenance's Strategic Advisory Board as Partner at Bain & Company; the record's own account is Advisor to Provenance since December 2025 and External Advisor to Bain since January 2026. Both are kept: the reports date the board's announcement, not his start, and use a Bain title he no longer held.

Native's post of 18 February 2026 says it ranked first on Spider 2.0; the benchmark's leaderboard, as read on 18 October 2026, ranks Native mini second (96.53, dated 18 February 2026) behind Genloop's Sentinel Agent v2 Pro (96.70), which the table dates 1 March 2026, eleven days after the post. The table's own dates are consistent with first place on the day of the post; the post's claim is kept as dated and company-reported.

Native's post of 2 October 2026 describes its 4B model as third among single-model entries on the BIRD hidden test set; the leaderboard's Single Trained Model Track, as read on 18 October 2026, numbers it 6, with 76.86 in the Test column and no Dev score. Of the five entries above it, two are dated before the post (12 March and 3 June 2026), one three days before it (29 September 2026) and two after it (10 October 2026); the track does not say when each row was added.

changelog.summary: Record format 4.1: every item carries a citation URL, its readable passage on the HTML page /profile; the biography lists the claims each sentence rests on; claims carry locators into their sources; the three Bain articles cite their own pages, with bylines and co-authors; robots.txt states the whole policy in every crawler group; the front page gains a link to the HTML page and a description.

Record format 4.0: organisations as their own list; atomic claims, outcomes, recognitions, corrections, featured links and section coverage; every item carries Brock's approval state and a visibility level. Drafts awaiting his decision stay out of production.

Record format 3.1: every item carries the day it was recorded and the day Brock last reviewed it; this change history is structured; profile.json validates against a published JSON Schema at profile.schema.json.

Record format 3.0: the HTML pages are gone; profile.json is the site, with profile.jsonld (a schema.org graph), profile.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a feed and an API catalog. The front page keeps its one line and gains a pointer, naming him, to profile.json.

Research intake: Illinois Tech advisory council membership; servicePath, Provenance and MAUSTRAP appearances; a Business Insider mention; three perspectives; Native and this site as projects; six questions and answers; each with its source, verified by opening the page.
Record format 2.0: sections for writing, speaking and events, projects, perspectives, press, credentials, memberships, questions and answers, a timeline, llms-full.txt and this feed.

Full career from LinkedIn: McKinsey, every dunnhumby role, early career. Sources cited as links on every item; Bain & Company's archived team page and three Bain articles added; LinkedIn as the verified profile.
Site live on brockdsimon.com with the original front page kept.
